nodes.author: Olaf Ronneberger

nodes.label: Binary U-Net Model (2 classes: background + leaf)
nodes.rationale: Instance labels (leaf 1,2,3,...) are not semantically consistent across images, so a standard U-Net cannot learn them as classes; converting to binary foreground-vs-background is what standard U-Net handles well.

nodes.label: BinaryLeafDataset
nodes.rationale: Converts instance masks (0..27) to binary on-the-fly with (mask > 0) so original mask files on disk are never modified; uses NEAREST resize to preserve label integrity.

nodes.label: Weighted BCE + Dice Combined Loss
nodes.rationale: BCE provides pixel-level gradient signal while Dice provides region-level overlap optimization; together they produce smooth, complete leaf masks.

nodes.label: Inverse Frequency Class Weighting
nodes.rationale: With >99% background pixels unweighted BCE learns to predict background everywhere; weight = total/(2*n_class) clamped to [0.3, 3.0] makes misclassifying a leaf pixel cost ~10x more.

nodes.label: Two-Stage Approach (Binary Segmentation + Watershed)
nodes.rationale: Stage 1 gives pixel-wise background/leaf mask; Stage 2 Watershed separates overlapping leaves into instance labels 1..N.

nodes.label: Marker Generation
nodes.rationale: Threshold at 40% of max distance then connected components gives one seed per leaf; lower to 25% for heavier overlap.

nodes.label: Mixed Precision Training (AMP)
nodes.rationale: Float16 softmax+CrossEntropy can overflow to NaN, so the loop checks gradients before stepping and skips problematic batches.

nodes.label: Dice-Based Early Stopping & Model Selection
nodes.rationale: IoU is the final metric of interest but Dice is more stable for small foreground regions during training; best_dice initialized to -1.0 so epoch 1 always saves.

nodes.label: Instance vs Semantic Segmentation
nodes.rationale: Leaf instance IDs are arbitrary per image so U-Net cannot treat them as semantic classes; binary conversion avoids the instance segmentation requirement.

U-Net Encoder-Decoder Architecture
nodes.rationale: U-Net is an encoder-decoder architecture with skip connections designed for biomedical image segmentation. The encoder extracts hierarchical features via downsampling; the decoder reconstructs spatial detail via upsampling. Skip connections preserve fine-grained detail by linking encoder features to corresponding decoder levels.

nodes.label: Skip Connections
nodes.rationale: Skip connections concatenate encoder feature maps with decoder feature maps at the same spatial resolution, preserving spatial detail that would otherwise be lost through downsampling.

nodes.label: Dice Loss + BCE Combined Loss
nodes.rationale: BCE provides stable per-pixel gradients early in training; Dice loss directly optimizes overlap robust to class imbalance. Combining both yields stable convergence and strong overlap metrics.

nodes.label: Automatic Mixed Precision (AMP)
nodes.rationale: AMP reduces memory by ~50% and increases throughput 1.5-2x via FP16 on GPU Tensor Cores, but fp16 overflow (>65504 logits) can cause NaN after convergence (~0.95 Dice), so it is disabled in production configs.

nodes.label: BinaryLeafDataset
nodes.rationale: Wraps multi-class masks (0-27 leaf types) into binary (0=background, 1=leaf) for binary segmentation training.

nodes.label: Attention Gates
nodes.rationale: Applied in skip connections before concatenation in the Up block to focus the decoder on foreground (leaf) regions, suppressing irrelevant background features.

nodes.label: Class Weighting (Inverse Frequency)
nodes.rationale: Foreground (leaf) pixels are fewer than background, so inverse-frequency weighting gives higher weight to the minority class. Clamping to [0.3, 3.0] prevents extreme weights from destabilizing training.

nodes.label: Gradient Checkpointing
nodes.rationale: Recomputes forward activations during backward pass instead of storing all layer activations. Trades 20-30% more compute for 40-50% GPU memory reduction.

nodes.label: Uniform Target Size 256x256 for Batch Stacking
Instance Segmentation
nodes.rationale: Semantic multiclass segmentation cannot separate overlapping leaf instances. Instance segmentation assigns unique IDs to each individual leaf, enabling counting and per-leaf measurement.

nodes.label: Mask Color-to-Instance Conversion
nodes.rationale: Current masks use ~13 recurring colors to represent leaves. Since colors are per-image palette (not consistent class labels), they must be remapped to per-instance IDs before instance-level training or evaluation.

nodes.label: Watershed Post-processing
nodes.rationale: Combines predicted binary mask with predicted distance map to separate overlapping leaf instances via watershed segmentation. This is the recommended approach for separating touching/overlapping leaves.

nodes.label: Standard BCE Loss Configuration
nodes.rationale: Baseline config using plain CrossEntropyLoss without class weighting or Dice component. AMP is disabled because fp16 overflow causes NaN after model convergence at ~0.95 Dice.

nodes.label: Weighted BCE + Dice Loss Configuration
nodes.rationale: Proposed config adding inverse-frequency class weighting (clamp 0.3-3.0) and Dice loss component on top of CrossEntropy, designed to address class imbalance between leaf and background pixels.
